purpose: A current-HEAD, matched-input verdict-agreement calibration screen for Grok and GPT-5.6 Sol. It reports agreement and frozen-design-intent error patterns on a small public-synthetic protocol; it is not an interchangeability, quality, or alignment study.

candidate_condition.rule: Any added judge condition is reported separately and does not alter the Sol-versus-Grok screen.

same_input_invariant: For a case/repetition, every enabled condition receives byte-identical artifact, target leaf, prompt, schema, context, and frozen runtime inputs.
historical_context: Earlier aggregate Grok/Sol evidence is intentionally not numerically restated here until its public artifact and exact binding are separately identified. It remains separate historical context, not a result of this current-HEAD protocol.
interpretation_limits: Grok is a development screen only. Sol remains canonical for scope, craft, penalty, and release decisions.
This screen has no single-leaf score or rank metric; a one-leaf result is a verdict calibration, not a cross-rubric score.
This screen freezes one provider attempt per singleton; it has no retry or validation-feedback prompt path.
run_judge does not emit a structured latency field, scope classification, or materiality classification. The analysis reports those limitations rather than importing a free-form sidecar.

This scaffold makes no remote call. Execution remains disabled until a trusted execution successor separately binds provider-neutral disclosure, external acknowledgement, zero-charge routes, launcher/backend identity, and a no-resend lifecycle.
